transcript: John Krasinski was People Magazine's Sexiest Man Alive in 2024. In 2025, he is playing the quintessential mediocre white man in Penelope Skinner's darkly comic play Angry Alan at Studio Seaview. Divorced and feeling disenfranchised, he falls into an internet rabbit hole of red pill content, finding a newfound sense of purpose and I'd say audacity. Initially, I thought this character would be impossible to empathize with, but John Krasinski brings a humour and complexity to the role that makes the show quite blurry in terms of tone. It's funny, but it's also kind of concerning and sad, and although the direct narration makes the whole thing a little heavy-handed, it forces us into a deep dive of a character that I imagine much of the audience might otherwise struggle to invest in. I thought John Krasinski was great — he kept our attention the entire time and the show was well-paced and well-directed, to the credit of Sam Gold. Angry Alan is running a Studio Seaview in Midtown until early August. With that, another program for my collection.
